To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new NMR methodology to determine 13C natural isotope ratios at the 1‰ level, with a better immunity to T1 variations than the initial DWET sequence.

the combination of optimized 1H NRM sequences (Multi-WET and Profile-WET) with a highly quantitative 13C internal reference method leads to a 13C irm-NMR method with 1‰ accuracy, which can be used for irm-13CNMR experiments with high relaxing agent concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new NMR methods for irm-13CNMR experiments.
the development of NMR methods to determine the 13C natural isotope abundance profile of a molecule, which is a key information to trace the (bio)synthesis pathway of a molecule.
the development of optimized pulse sequences to perform 1H quantitative NMR experiments and their combination with irm-13C to determine 13C isotopomers profiles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new DWET pulse sequences are more robust to T1 variations and pulse miscalibrating, and are therefore more suitable to perform irm-13C experiments.
the Multi-WET and the Profiled-WET are both optimized pulse sequences for irm-13NMR.

the DWET sequence is the most robust and accurate method to determine the 13C intraposition-specific isotopic composition of organic molecules at natural abundance, and it is the method of choice for PSIA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Multi-WET and profiled-WET pulse sequences are the first quantitative 1H pulse sequences that are robust to variations in T1, which is an essential requirement for irm-13CNMR experiments.
the Multi-WET and the Profiled-WET pulse sequences are optimized to perform irm-13C analysis on compounds with a short T1, thus opening the door for irm-13NMR experiments in the field of PSIA.

the Multi-WET and the Profiled-WET are the first quantitative 1H pulse sequences which are robust to T1 variations and thus can be used to measure the 13C position-specific abundance xi in presence of relaxing agent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
irm-13C is now a reliable and robust technique for PSIA.
the Multi-WET sequence is more robust than Profiled-WET to pulse miscalibration and to T1 variations and is therefore the best choice for irm-13NMR applications.
the use of a 1H NRM experiment is not only a powerful way to improve quantitative accuracy but also a way to increase the robustness of the experiment towards T1 variation.
